<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914059_theRebbe_310" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914059_theRebbe_310__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Yom Kippur contains both the revelation of the essence of the soul connected to Atzmus and its manifestation in the soul's particular levels, corresponding to the five prayers.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that also on Yom Kippur there are these two matters,</t>
    <t s="3">the revelation of the essence of the soul that is connected to the Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="4">and that this matter is revealed in the particular levels of the soul,</t>
    <t s="5">down to the level of Nefesh within it,</t>
    <t s="6">through which atonement is revealed</t>
    <t s="7">(in the aforementioned manner)</t>
    <t s="8">also in the levels of the soul in which defect is applicable.</t>
    <t s="9">And this is that Yom Kippur is a day that is obligated in five prayers,</t>
    <t s="10">the five prayers correspond to the five names of the soul,</t>
    <t s="11">Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="12">and the matter of a day obligated in five prayers is that the revelation of the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="13">which is from the essence of the day itself,</t>
    <t s="14">is revealed in its particular levels.</t>
    <t s="15">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="16">that the difference between the five prayers is not only in the place</t>
    <t s="17">(the level)</t>
    <t s="18">in which the essence of the soul is revealed,</t>
    <t s="19">but also in the revelation itself.</t>
    <t s="20">For in the Neilah prayer,</t>
    <t s="21">the aspect of Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="22">the revelation is greater than in the four prayers before it.</t>
    <t s="23">And likewise regarding the four prayers themselves,</t>
    <t s="24">the difference is also in the manner of the revelation.</t>
    <t s="25">And likewise in the aspects above,</t>
    <t s="26">that Yom Kippur is a day obligated in five prayers is because on Yom Kippur there is the ascent of Malchus into Atik</t>
    <t s="27">(as explained in the Siddur),</t>
    <t s="28">that this matter is throughout the entire day,</t>
    <t s="29">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="30">there are in this several levels,</t>
    <t s="31">and the main ascent is at Neilah</t>
    <t s="32">(as explained in the Siddur).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The levels of Yom Kippur are divided into two general levels, "Shabbos Shabbason hi" (feminine) in Atik of the three heads, and "Shabbos Shabbason hu" (masculine) in the Ein Sof of Rada"la.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now the levels of Yom Kippur are divided into two general levels.</t>
    <t s="1">"Shabbos Shabbason hi" (it is a Sabbath of solemn rest, feminine)</t>
    <t s="2">(feminine language)</t>
    <t s="3">and "Shabbos Shabbason hu" (it is a Sabbath of solemn rest, masculine)</t>
    <t s="4">(masculine language).</t>
    <t s="5">For the two levels are in Atik,</t>
    <t s="6">except that there are two interpretations of Atik.</t>
    <t s="7">That in general,</t>
    <t s="8">the upper aspect of Kesser</t>
    <t s="9">(and specifically the three heads within it)</t>
    <t s="10">is called by the name Atik,</t>
    <t s="11">but the essential matter of Atik is the Ein Sof that is within the three heads.</t>
    <t s="12">And the difference between the two aforementioned levels is,</t>
    <t s="13">that "Shabbos Shabbason hi"</t>
    <t s="14">(feminine language)</t>
    <t s="15">is in Atik,</t>
    <t s="16">in its three heads</t>
    <t s="17">(in which Rada"la is also included),</t>
    <t s="18">and "Shabbos Shabbason hu"</t>
    <t s="19">(masculine language)</t>
    <t s="20">is in the Ein Sof of Rada"la.</t>
    <t s="21">And based on this, an additional explanation can be given regarding that after it says "Shuva Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha,"</t>
    <t s="22">for "ad" (until) and not including "ad" is in Atik</t>
    <t s="23">(as brought above in section 3 from Likkutei Torah),</t>
    <t s="24">and that "Hashem as Elokim is considered" regarding the Ein Sof that is above Havayah, it can be said that this is regarding the Ein Sof of Rada"la.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The advantage of Yom Kippur being obligated in five prayers is that the revelation of the soul's essence in its particular levels enables atonement, especially for simple sins, demonstrating the unlimited bond of Israel with Hashem.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that this that they say the virtue of Yom Kippur is,</t>
    <t s="3">that it is a day obligated in five prayers,</t>
    <t s="4">even though the day itself</t>
    <t s="5">(the revelation of the connection of the essence of the soul with Atzmus)</t>
    <t s="6">is more elevated than this being obligated in five prayers</t>
    <t s="7">(the revelation in the particular levels of the soul),</t>
    <t s="8">it is,</t>
    <t s="9">because this that the essence of the soul is revealed in its particular levels,</t>
    <t s="10">through which there is atonement in the place where there was initially the defect,</t>
    <t s="11">has an advantage over the level of the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="12">For although in the aspects of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah and particularly the aspect of Nefesh</t>
    <t s="13">(as they are in themselves)</t>
    <t s="14">defects are applicable, nevertheless they are atoned for.</t>
    <t s="15">[And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="16">that the atonement from the essence of the day is in a manner that it is revealed that in their innerness there was no defect from the outset,</t>
    <t s="17">as above].</t>
    <t s="18">And likewise regarding the matter of atonement itself,</t>
    <t s="19">that the main novelty in atonement is atonement for simple sins.</t>
    <t s="20">For atonement for the sins of tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="21">the matter of "there is one who loves" and the like, which relative to their level is like casting off the yoke,</t>
    <t s="22">since regarding these sins it cannot be said that they are the opposite of the will of the Holy One, blessed be He</t>
    <t s="23">[for this selfhood is due to the nature that the Holy One, blessed be He, implanted],</t>
    <t s="24">therefore,</t>
    <t s="25">the atonement for this is not such a novelty.</t>
    <t s="26">And the main novelty and</t>
    <t s="27">(consequently)</t>
    <t s="28">the advantage is in atonement for simple sins,</t>
    <t s="29">for in this is revealed the unlimited power of the bond of Yisrael and the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="30">that even when they did the opposite of His will, nevertheless</t>
    <t s="31">(through repentance and atonement)</t>
    <t s="32">they are pleasing before Him, blessed be He, as if they had never sinned.</t>
    <t s="33">And this is that our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="34">"In the place where penitents stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand,"</t>
    <t s="35">it can be said that this statement of our sages does not depart from its simple meaning,</t>
    <t s="36">and the main advantage of penitents is in simple penitents.</t>
    <t s="37">And based on this, what the Tzemach Tzedek brings</t>
    <t s="38">(from the book Taamei HaMitzvos of the AriZal) will be understood,</t>
    <t s="39">that this that the AriZal was accustomed to recite specific confessions is,</t>
    <t s="40">because all of Yisrael are one body,</t>
    <t s="41">for ostensibly it could be said that the confessions of the AriZal were about matters of extreme subtlety that were applicable even to him</t>
    <t s="42">[and in the manner explained above regarding the selfhood of "there is one who loves"],</t>
    <t s="43">and this that they explain that the confessions of the AriZal were</t>
    <t s="44">(also)</t>
    <t s="45">for simple sins because all of Yisrael are one body,</t>
    <t s="46">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="47">for according to this explanation specifically it is understood that by the AriZal there was also the advantage of simple penitents.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
